title: Conditions, equality and explicit missing decisions
outcome: Write explicit Boolean decisions and select equality semantics appropriate to numeric values and data keys.

exercises.title: Distinguish zero and absent
exercises.task: Compare rates 0/5 and 0/0 under the helper policy.
exercises.expected: The first is 0; the second is nothing.
exercises.answer: A real zero rate is different from having no valid denominator.

exercises.title: Check a predicate
exercises.task: Use an integer directly as an if condition.
exercises.answer: The language requires a Boolean decision rather than an implicit truthiness conversion.

exercises.title: Protect an access
exercises.task: Guard the first element of a possibly empty array.
exercises.expected: The access occurs only when the collection is nonempty.
exercises.hint: Put the guard first in a short-circuit expression.
exercises.answer: This makes the precondition visible and prevents a predictable boundary error.

exercises.title: Compare NaN keys
exercises.task: Use isequal for two NaN values.
exercises.expected: The data-key equality result is true.
exercises.hint: Do not substitute ordinary numerical equality.
exercises.answer: Dictionary-oriented equality needs consistent treatment of special values.

exercises.title: Inspect signed zero
exercises.task: Compare 0.0 and -0.0 using both equality functions.
exercises.hint: The sign bit can matter for key semantics.
exercises.answer: Choose the relation required by the application rather than assuming all equality operations are interchangeable.

exercises.title: Keep an unknown decision
exercises.answer: A data policy must decide whether to reject, defer or explicitly replace the unknown value.
